anautomat 1.0.0 adds on-device Java execution and fast, guarded device macros.

- The agent writes restricted Java 8 method bodies, compiles them on Android, converts them to DEX and runs them in a fresh permissionless isolated process. No JavaScript runtime, PC bridge, downloaded runtime or on-device JDK installation is required.
- Generated bytecode is checked against an explicit API allowlist. Reflection, file/network APIs, Android APIs, native methods, process/thread creation and dynamic bytecode are rejected. Build/runtime deadlines and heap-growth watchdogs bound each invocation.
- Java can compute results, retain bounded JSON state within a Goal, log output and generate macros. A macro executes up to 32 validated operations without a model request between them. Touch/text operations require the expected app package; literal-text guards and settling delays are available.
- Pause, failure or timeout discards unfinished operations. Manual resume captures a fresh screen; an old batch is never replayed automatically. Java execution can be disabled in Settings.
- Full third-party notices and English/Japanese controls are included. Compiler/dexer downloads retain SHA-256 pins, advisory audits and a seven-day supply-chain cooldown.

The live Android smoke test completed a Java computation and a three-operation macro in two model steps, then verified the result on screen. JVM and native tests cover forbidden APIs, loop/memory termination, JSON limits, macro ordering and cancellation. See docs/automation.md and docs/automation-evidence.md for APIs, boundaries and test evidence.

Install over your existing production release to retain sign-in and settings, or use the app’s Updates card. Android still requires installation confirmation. Already completed device operations cannot be rolled back, and an in-flight Android gesture may finish after pause.
